chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu al-Maghra', from Abu Basir who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever forgets a chapter of the Quran, it will be embodied for him in a beautiful form in a lofty station in Paradise. When he sees it, he will say: "What are you? How beautiful you are! If only you were mine!" So it will say: "Do you not recognize me? I am Surah such-and-such. Had you not forgotten me, I would have raised you to this (station)."'

key_terms.درجة رفيعة: A lofty rank or station in Paradise, indicating the spiritual reward associated with preserving Quranic memorization
key_terms.سورة: A complete chapter of the Quran, with its own name, spiritual significance, and intercessive power
key_terms.مُثِّلَتْ: Was personified/embodied — a passive form indicating that the surah is given a physical manifestation by God
key_terms.نسي: To forget, in classical Islamic usage often implies willful neglect or abandonment rather than accidental forgetting

ai.seo_question: What happens to a person who forgets a Quran chapter after memorizing it?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) warns of the spiritual consequences of neglecting and forgetting the Quran. In this eschatological hadith, a forgotten Quranic surah is personified in Paradise as a beautiful being occupying a high station, reproaching the one who memorized it but then let it slip away. The imagery conveys that memorized Quranic chapters are not mere texts but living spiritual presences that accompany their reciters in the Hereafter — and that neglecting them constitutes a real loss of divine elevation.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Al Magra’a, from Abu baser who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who forgets a Chapter from the Quran, it would be resembled for him in a beautiful image, and be in a lofty level in the Paradise. So when he sees it, he would say, ‘What are you? How beautiful! If only you were for me’. So it would be saying: ‘But, do you not recognise me? I am Chapter such and such, and had you not forgotten me, I would have raised you to this (level)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu al- Maghra’ from abu Basir who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘If one forgets a chapter from the Holy Quran it will appear to him in the best form and high position in paradise. When he will see it he will say how beautiful you are! I wish you were mine.’ It will ask, ‘Do you not know me? I am chapter so and so, had you not forgotten me I would have raised you to this.’”
